direct_answer: Heart failure and arthritis can both limit activity and cause tiredness. Pacing, gentle exercise as advised and medicine reviews help. Some arthritis medicines, such as anti-inflammatories, may not be suitable with heart failure, so check with your GP or pharmacist.

content:
Living with two conditions that both drain energy means planning your day carefully.

This guide covers practical pacing and safety. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Pacing

  • Plan tasks and rest.
  • Spread activity across the day.
  • Use aids to save energy.

Medicines

Anti-inflammatory painkillers (NSAIDs) can worsen heart failure. Check with your pharmacist before buying any over-the-counter pain relief.

Exercise

Cardiac rehabilitation or a physiotherapist can advise on safe activity.

Swollen legs and ankles

  • Swelling has many causes, including heart, kidney or vein problems and some medicines.
  • Raise your legs and move your ankles regularly.
  • Tell your GP about new or worsening swelling, especially in one leg.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, sudden severe breathlessness, or if one leg is suddenly swollen, red, warm and painful.
  • Contact your GP or heart failure team if you gain weight quickly or your breathlessness or swelling gets worse.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Can I take ibuprofen?

Ask your GP or pharmacist first.

Is exercise safe?

Usually, with advice.
